You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE employee (
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    City TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE shop (
    Shop_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Location TEXT,
    District TEXT,
    Number_products INT,
    Manager_name TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE hiring (
    Shop_ID INT,
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Start_from TEXT,
    Is_full_time bool,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Shop_ID) REFERENCES shop(Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE evaluation (
    Employee_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Year_awarded TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Bonus REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID)
);

How do you want to define **“hard-working”** in this database? There isn’t a column for that, so we need a rule, for example:

1) Employees who received a **bonus** (evaluation.Bonus > 0) in a given year  
2) Employees with the **highest bonuses** (top N)  
3) Employees with **multiple years** of bonuses  
4) Full-time employees (**hiring.Is_full_time = true**)

Meanwhile, here are a few ready-to-run SQL options you can pick from.

### A) Employees who received any bonus (treat as hard-working)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 0
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC;
```

### B) Top 10 “hard-working” employees by total bonus (all years)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  SUM(ev.Bonus) AS total_bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
GROUP BY e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City
ORDER BY total_bonus DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### C) Employees with bonuses in 2+ different years
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ev.Year_awarded) AS bonus_years,
  SUM(ev.Bonus) AS total_bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 0
GROUP BY e.Employee_ID, e.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ev.Year_awarded) >= 2
ORDER BY total_bonus DESC;
```

### D) Full-time employees (if that’s your meaning)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  h.Shop_ID,
  h.Start_from
FROM employee e
JOIN hiring h
  ON h.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
WHERE h.Is_full_time = 1;   -- or TRUE depending on your SQL dialect
```

Tell me which definition you want (A/B/C/D, or your own), and if you want to filter by a specific **shop**, **year**, or **district**.
I want to look at the employee who got the most in one-time bonuses.

To get the employee who received the **largest single (one-time) bonus** in any year:

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

If you want **all ties** (multiple employees with the same max bonus):

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus = (SELECT MAX(Bonus) FROM evaluation);
```
make sure to fetch the name of the employee who got the highest one-time bonus

```sql
SELECT
  e.Name,
  ev.Bonus AS highest_one_time_bonus
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
focus on the employee who received the highest amount in that category

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus AS highest_one_time_bonus
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus = (SELECT MAX(Bonus) FROM evaluation);
```
